name: jevlint-le
description: Lint the questions you send to TypeSafe's Jev model and OpenAI's Decisions API (gpt-6-luna) as you type, with no API key and no network calls. An optional command asks Jev or Luna itself to check a file

untrustedWorkspaces.description: Linting works everywhere. Checking a file with Jev sends its questions to TypeSafe and is disabled in an untrusted workspace.

commands.title: Lint Jev Questions in This File
Lint Jev Questions in the Workspace
Check This File with Jev (uses your API key)
Probe the Jev Question at the Cursor (uses your API key)

jevlint-le.rules.markdownDescription: Severity per rule code. Values: `off`, `hint`, `info`, `warning`, `error`. A rule not listed keeps its default. Example: `{ "JEV004": "off" }`.

jevlint-le.fallbackOptions.markdownDescription: Words that make a Choice option a fallback for `JEV004`. An option counts when one of these is a word in its name, matched case-insensitively with `_` and `-` read as spaces, so `none_implied` counts under `none`.

jevlint-le.ignore.markdownDescription: Findings to drop, as `CODE:questionId`. Example: `JEV004:department`. This is the way to suppress a finding in JSON, which has no comments.

jevlint-le.include.markdownDescription: Glob of files the workspace command lints.

jevlint-le.exclude.markdownDescription: Glob of files the workspace command skips.

jevlint-le.maxFileSizeBytes.markdownDescription: Files larger than this are reported as skipped, not linted.

jevlint-le.jev.model.markdownDescription: The model the **Check This File with Jev** command asks: a Jev version, or `gpt-6-luna` for OpenAI's Decisions API, which then uses your OpenAI key. Pinned to the version its checks were calibrated on. An alias such as `jev-latest` will move those cutoffs under you, and a finding from Luna says the cutoff was set on Jev.

jevlint-le.jev.maxCalls.markdownDescription: The most requests one **Check This File with Jev** run may send. Each question in the file costs one request. Questions past the limit are counted and not sent.

jevlint-le.jev.sendState.markdownDescription: Also send the `state` written beside a `questions` map, so Jev can check whether the state holds what each question asks about and whether it carries instructions. Off by default: with it off, only questions are sent. It applies only where the state is written out in the file.

jevlint-le.jev.confirm.markdownDescription: Before **Check This File with Jev** or the probe sends anything, show how many requests it will make, roughly what that costs and whether your state is sent, and wait for a yes. Off by default: running the command is taken as the decision to send.

jevlint-le.jev.apiKey.markdownDescription: Your TypeSafe API key, for **Check This File with Jev** and the probe. It can only be set in your user settings, never in a workspace, so it cannot end up in a repository, and it is left out of Settings Sync. **Set TypeSafe API Key** in the command palette stores it in the system keychain instead, which keeps it out of a plain-text file. A key set here is used ahead of one in the keychain.

jevlint-le.jev.openaiApiKey.markdownDescription: Your OpenAI API key, used by **Check This File with Jev** when `jevlint-le.jev.model` is `gpt-6-luna`. Held the same way as the TypeSafe key: user settings only, left out of Settings Sync, and **Set OpenAI API Key** stores it in the system keychain instead.

enumDescriptions: Show every message, including the summary after each command.
Hide the summaries. Still say when a run was cancelled or files were left out.
Show a message only when a command you ran could not do anything.
jevlint-le.notificationsLevel.markdownDescription: How much JevLint-LE tells you in notifications. Findings always appear in the editor and the Problems panel, whatever this is set to.
